subject: Post-call: streaming model fit & UX concerns
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: streaming model fit & UX concerns

Thanks again for the demo today - appreciate the time. A quick recap from our side and the asks you'd promised to follow up on:

- Observed issues during the prototype: partial output coherence (sentences cut off mid-thought in the stream), inconsistent handling of our stop token (we use '###' to end assistant output), and a few token-level latency spikes (~250-400ms) that cause a choppy UX in our client.
- We sent a short prompt sample and a few session transcripts during the call; attaching the prompt set we used (acme_stream_prompts.csv).

What we need from Redwood to evaluate next:
1) Which model(s) you recommend for our use-case (real-time clinician assistant): balancing coherence, short-response latency, and strict stop-sequence handling.
2) Any benchmark links or eval artifacts you can share for streaming behaviour.
3) Suggested next steps for a canary / pilot (metrics to watch, data to collect).

Happy to hop on another 30-min call next week. Thanks - Alicia

Attachment: acme_stream_prompts.csv (csv, 12 rows)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: streaming model fit & UX concerns

Hi Alicia - great notes, and thanks for the prompt set. Short answers up front and a proposed plan below.

Recommended models (start here):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized): best latency/cost balance, good instruction-following for short dialogs.
- Llama2-13B-chat (int8 quant): stronger coherence on longer contexts if you need more detailed assistant responses; expect higher token-latency but better completion quality.

Notes on stop-sequence handling:
- We observed stop-token regressions historically when the model and tokenizer have ambiguous tokens; we'll run a tokenizer alignment pass on your prompt set to ensure '###' is tokenized as expected and add a forced-stop policy in streaming to guarantee termination on that sequence.

Benchmark artifacts: here's a runbook & recent streaming evals: https://drive.redwood.com/Acme/benchmarks/2026-10-streaming-eval (contains per-model latency, partial-output incidence, and stop-sequence checks).

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Redwood runs a 3-day focused streaming eval on your prompt set (we'll produce per-token latency histograms + partial-output rate).
2) We implement a forced-stop policy and tokenizer alignment on the top candidate model.
3) Canary deployment (1 week, limited traffic) instrumented with session traces and an SLO dashboard.

I've attached a short checklist we use for canaries. Can you confirm target SLOs (e.g., p95 per-token latency target, stop-sequence correctness %) and availability of 1 week of production-like traffic for the canary?

Thanks - I'll have Jordan add more technical detail and a sample eval report.

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: (see drive link above)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: streaming model fit & UX concerns

Hi Alicia - adding the technical detail we discussed. Attached is a short eval summary (streaming_eval_results.pdf) from a recent run that mirrors your prompt distribution. Highlights:
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (quant, tuned): median per-token latency ~120ms, p95 ~220ms; partial-output incidents ~1.8% of sessions (mostly due to mid-response trimming when clients request early stop).
- Llama2-13B-chat (int8): median ~180ms, p95 ~360ms; partial-output incidents ~0.9% but higher cost.

Stop sequences:
- We ran a tokenizer alignment and flagged ambiguous tokenizations of close-char sequences. For '###' we recommend a forced-stop policy that flushes the output buffer as soon as the sequence is emitted by the LM. That reduces partial-output incidence by ~70% in our sandbox tests.

Attachments included: streaming_eval_results.pdf, acme_prompt_set_v1.json (sample prompt set used for the eval).

Next steps from engineering side:
- We'll run the eval on your exact prompt CSV and push a canary image with forced-stop and reduced chunking size (smaller streaming chunks reduce perceived latency at the cost of throughput).
- We will instrument per-token latency and a stop-sequence mismatch metric in the dashboard.

--
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: streaming_eval_results.pdf (PDF), acme_prompt_set_v1.json (json, 42 entries)

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: streaming model fit & UX concerns

Thanks, Jordan and Marissa - this is helpful. Couple clarifications from product/UX: 

- Target SLOs: p95 per-token latency should be <= 200ms for clinician-facing short prompts (single-turn responses of up to 80 tokens). If you think Mistral hits that most reliably, great - otherwise we need to consider engineering mitigations.
- Stop token enforcement: critical. Our UI depends on a hard delimiter '###' to mark end-of-response so partial emissions are a functional bug.
- Can you estimate how the forced-stop policy impacts end-to-end latency vs. perceived UX? We can run a short canary with 5k sample sessions.

Also - procurement question: what's the typical pilot pricing for a 1-week canary (5k sessions)? Tom, can you confirm whether Acme prefers a PO or credit-card trial?

Thanks - Alicia

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: streaming model fit & UX concerns

Alicia - thanks, and noted. Attached is a one-page mutual action plan that lays out responsibilities, timeline, and data we need from your side (sample session logs + the anonymized prompt pairs). We can commit to the following for the pilot:

- Redwood will run a 3-day model-fit eval on your prompt set, then a 1-week canary with forced-stop and smaller chunk size.
- p95 per-token latency target: we'll aim for <=200ms on Mistral-Instruct-7B; if we miss, we'll switch to Llama2-13B-chat for the canary and quantify cost delta.
- Success criteria: p95 per-token <=200ms AND stop-sequence mismatch <0.5% across canary traffic.

Pricing & procurement: for a one-week, 5k-session pilot we typically apply a pilot credit (we can cover up to $X of usage) and work with procurement for a PO if you want to scale. Tom - want me to loop in our finance lead for a formal quote?

Next steps:
1) Acme provides anonymized session logs + confirm which of the attached prompt CSV rows are representative.
2) Redwood kick off the eval (we'll send a test dashboard link within 48 hours).
3) Schedule a 30-min sync at the start of the canary; I sent a Doodle earlier - can we target the week of Nov 9?

Attachment: mutual_action_plan.docx

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
